exploitContext: Live exploit reported on batchMint: attacker 'could supply too many params'. In BatchNFTMinter.batchMint the only caller-influenced multiplicity is the scalar `count`, which directly bounds the unguarded loop at line 207. There are NO array parameters in either in-scope contract (verified via grep for `[]`/`.length`), so 'mismatched array length' and 'array-length cap' patterns are structurally inapplicable; the live exploit maps to an unbounded loop count.

findings.description: batchMint loops `for (uint256 i; i < count; ++i)` over the caller-supplied `count` with no upper bound (only `count == 0` is rejected at line 191). Each iteration performs an external `nftMinter.mint(dispatcherIndex, recipient)` call (line 208), so total gas scales linearly and unboundedly with `count`. A caller who supplies an excessively large `count` ('too many params') causes the batch to exceed the block gas limit and revert, and — combined with the upfront `paymentToken.safeTransferFrom` pull (line 204) and `forceApprove(max)` (line 205) — wastes gas / can grief callers. This is the direct on-chain analogue of the reported live exploit: the multiplicity an attacker controls is the loop `count`, not any array length.
vulnerableConditionsMet: Loop bound (`count`) is fully caller-supplied with no maximum
No pagination / no per-call cap on `count`
No gas-limit guard; iteration body is an external CALL (mint) so per-iteration gas is non-trivial
missingMitigations: No require(count <= MAX) bound (contrast: count == 0 IS guarded at line 191, max is not)
findings.notes: Reachability: batchMint is external and whenNotPaused-gated only (no access control beyond pause), so any account can call with an arbitrary count. The unbounded count is also a self-DoS / fat-finger vector (caller burns gas to a revert) and a griefing vector when count is chosen to land near the block gas limit. Manual review should confirm intended impact tier: as a pure gas-bound revert with no fund loss this is MEDIUM per the pattern DB; escalate only if a concrete value-loss path is demonstrated (none found in static review). NOTE: NFTStaker.sol contains no loops or array parameters and produces no DOS-UNBOUNDED-LOOP match.

patternsConsideredAndCleared.reason: No array parameters exist in either in-scope contract. `grep -nE '\[\]|\.length'` over BatchNFTMinter.sol and NFTStaker.sol returns no matches. batchMint takes only scalar/address args; recipient is a single address. The 'too many params' exploit therefore cannot be an array-length mismatch — it is the scalar loop count (PATTERN-001).

All token movements use SafeERC20 (safeTransferFrom L204, forceApprove L205/L211, safeTransfer L222/L230, NFTStaker safeTransfer/safeTransferFrom throughout). No raw .transfer/.send/.call on tokens. No medium-confidence match.

BatchNFTMinter.batchMint has no ReentrancyGuard and interleaves external calls (mint loop, nudge safeTransfer L222, dust sweep L230) with reads, but it holds no persistent per-user accounting that a reentrant call could corrupt: the nudge transfers live balanceOf and the dust sweep reads live balanceOf, so a reentrant batchMint would simply re-run the same balance-based logic atomically. NFTStaker uses nonReentrant on all user entrypoints. Token type is also not ERC777 in this system (phUSD / payment tokens). Below medium confidence; left for manual reviewer rather than reported.

onlyOwner setters and onlyPauser gating are present and documented as intentional owner/pauser trust assumptions in registered-projects.json knownIssues. Pattern DB marks this Low/QA; project known-issues cover it.

No address(this).balance logic and no payable/msg.value usage in scope; nudge/dust logic keys off ERC20 balanceOf, and a pre-deposit griefer is explicitly documented as merely donating to the next caller (BatchNFTMinter NatSpec L42-45).
